newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers says Serzone sleep better.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers says Serzone sleep better.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said that studies showed that nefazodone, the ingredient in its Serzone antidepressant, increased sleep efficiency in patients, while fluoxetine, the ingredient in Prozac, which is made by Eli Lilly and Co, reduced sleep efficiency.
Bristol said that nefazodone reduced the number of nighttime awakenings, while fluoxetine increased them.

The most common significant adverse events associated with nefazodone treatment in placebo-controlled trials include asthenia, or weakness, dry mouth, nausea, constipation, somnolence, dizziness, lightheadedness, confusion and visual symptoms, Bristol said.
A spokesman for Lilly said he had not seen the data, but noted sleep disorder is one of the symptoms of depression.
"Depression can disturb your sleep, not treatment for depression," he said.
